clearedSpotChecks.check: Transient storage path of the Nitro b72783f release binaries run in the cycle 30 x86-64 and AArch64 models (opTstore, opTload, SetTransientState, GetTransientState, journal append and revert, transientStorageChange revert) over 20007 sequences on the PoolManager delta, NonzeroDeltaCount, Lock and reserves slots.
clearedSpotChecks.note: out/ts-amd64.json records 20007 sequences, 448662 reads, 171624 stores, 29011 reverts, 4014 equal writes, zero mismatches and zero errors, and five planted-fault runs exist for each architecture. out/maptype.txt gives hasher and equal closure size 52 on both architectures, which matches the transientStorageKey struct {addr common.Address; key common.Hash} in go-ethereum v1.17.10 core/state/transient_storage.go; I fetched that file from raw.githubusercontent.com and its sha256 equals the local copy (b1a2e485...). Set deletes on a zero value and Get reads the struct key, so a delta slot keccak256(target, currency) cannot alias another account's slot. src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:18-23 and 28-40 read and write with plain tload and tstore, so the committed word is what the PoolManager sees. The Go map runtime calls were stubbed in the model, so map internals rest on the Go runtime rather than on this run; that is a standard component and not Arbitrum specific.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Live eth_call with state overrides on the deployed PoolManagers of Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain with settle, kept-revert and nested-revert variants matched pyevm reference bytes on both backend architectures.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I queried web3_clientVersion on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc and https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com and both returned nitro/v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f-20261116T155937Z/linux-arm64/go1.27.3, the build the cleared item names (blocks 0x1f77d251 and 0x7656322 at query time). eth_getCode of the PoolManager addresses in state/networks.json returned 24009 bytes with sha256 395c56a5... on 42161 and 6eb21c69... on 4663, equal to pmCodeSha256 in out/live-42161.json and out/live-4663.json, so the runs exercised the deployed bytecode. The live files record matching reference bytes for the settled variant. The two chains' codes differ in hash, which fits per-deployment immutables; the runs compared each chain against its own code.

clearedSpotChecks.check: isCode and the jump destination map in both binaries (L-1206): analysis cached per 32-byte code hash in a per-EVM map, initcode analysed locally, no SetJumpDestCache caller.
clearedSpotChecks.note: out/lst-amd64/vm.__Contract_.isCode.s shows a runtime.memequal against the field at contract+0x70 (the CodeHash), then two codeBitmapInternal paths after runtime.makeslice, one followed by an interface call for Store and one without, and only panicBounds and morestack on the remaining exits. That matches the structure of go-ethereum contract.go isCode: a zero code hash gets a local bitmap, a nonzero one is loaded or stored by hash. A shared bitmap between two codes then needs equal keccak256 hashes, so JUMP and JUMPI in the PoolManager and in the Hooks and Currency call targets are validated against their own code. I did not repeat the full-text xref scan for SetJumpDestCache callers.
